answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token as collateral before it can post jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by collateral actually locked, not by the number of accounts, so splitting one stake across a vine of aliases does not multiply voting power. If an identity is caught coordinating fraud, its stake is slashed and redistributed to harmed participants. A jade badge or orchard-themed profile adds no weight: the attacker must buy and risk more collateral for each additional unit of influence.
